data.narrative:
Lambda is a Series E AI & Software company that has raised $3.15B to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public (Palantir) and 8 private entities including Crusoe Energy, SandboxAQ, and Ayar Labs—all operating in the same sector and stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical for Series E advancement, yielding $4.4B. Peer-median benchmarking across the 4-company same-stage cohort produces a median valuation of $7.9B, though the peer range is wide ($3.8B to $312.5B) driven primarily by Palantir's public-market valuation of $312.5B. The lower-quartile peers (Ayar Labs at $3.8B, SandboxAQ at $5.8B) provide more granular positioning.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $3.7B to $9.1B, with a median point estimate of $6.1B. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound; peer-median analysis extends the upper bound. Key uncertainties center on peer comparability—particularly whether Lambda's operational profile aligns with the lower-quartile peers or commands a premium toward the broader cohort median. The wide dispersion in public-market AI valuations (Palantir) relative to early-stage private fundraising creates material sensitivity to stage-to-exit assumptions.
